name: Battles of Lexington and Concord
note: The plan shows the whole running fight along the road from Lexington to Concord and back to Charlestown, not a single field. Distances are only roughly to scale, and the accounts do not say which side of the road each hill and farm lay on; those are placed by judgement. The accounts differ on who fired the first shot at Lexington; the plan does not decide it.

terrain.name: Road to Concord
terrain.quote: Beyond the curves, the road straightened to the east, with cleared fields and orchards along the sides.

terrain.name: Concord
terrain.quote: Colonel Smith divided troops arriving at Concord to carry out Gage's orders

terrain.name: Old North Bridge
terrain.quote: led the men from the center of town across the Old North Bridge

terrain.name: Punkatasset Hill
terrain.quote: from their vantage point on Punkatasset Hill to a lower, closer flat hilltop

terrain.name: Lexington
terrain.quote: about 80 Lexington militiamen emerged from Buckman Tavern and stood in ranks on Lexington Common

terrain.name: Menotomy
terrain.quote: Fighting grew more intense as Percy's forces moved into Menotomy.

terrain.name: Charlestown
terrain.quote: eventually reached the safety of Charlestown after incurring heavy losses

units.name: Smith's main column
units.quote: The Regulars, around 700 infantrymen, were drawn from 11 of Gage's 13 occupying infantry regiments.

units.name: Advance guard, light infantry
units.quote: Colonel Smith ordered Major Pitcairn to quick march to Concord with six companies of light infantry.

units.name: Companies at the North Bridge
units.quote: At least 400 Patriots confronted Captain Laurie's light infantry companies, totaling 90–95 men.

units.name: Parsons' companies at the farm
units.quote: Captain Parsons took four companies from the 5th, 23rd, 38th, and 52nd Regiments up the road 2 miles (3.2 km) beyond the North Bridge

units.name: Percy's relief brigade
units.quote: A full British brigade, about 1,000 men with artillery, under the command of Earl Percy, had arrived.

units.name: Lexington militia
units.quote: Parker positioned his company in parade-ground formation, on Lexington Common in plain sight

units.name: Concord and Acton militia
units.quote: Five full companies of minutemen and five more of militiamen from Acton, Concord, Bedford and Lincoln occupied the hill.

units.name: Militia along the road
units.quote: Colonial militia companies arriving from the north and east converged here, clearly outnumbering the Regulars.

units.name: Russell farm militia
units.quote: Here hundreds of militiamen from towns further out had assembled over the course of the afternoon to await the appearance of the returning British column.

phases.title: The militia stand on Lexington Common
phases.text: About 80 Lexington militiamen formed up on the Common in plain sight, but not across the road to Concord. Pitcairn's advance guard entered Lexington, with Smith's remaining companies further down the road.
phases.quote: Parker positioned his company in parade-ground formation, on Lexington Common in plain sight (not behind walls), but not blocking the road to Concord.

phases.title: The Regulars charge and the militia disperse
phases.text: After shots were fired, of which the accounts disagree on the first, the Regulars charged with bayonets. Eight Lexington men were killed and ten wounded, and the militia fell back.
phases.quote: After the shots were fired, the Regulars charged forward with bayonets.

phases.title: The Regulars search Concord
phases.text: Smith reformed the column and marched to Concord, where he divided it to search for supplies. Four companies under Captain Parsons went beyond the North Bridge, while Laurie's companies guarded it. Barrett's militia watched from a hill to the north.
phases.quote: Colonel Smith divided troops arriving at Concord to carry out Gage's orders to search for supplies.

phases.title: The fight at the North Bridge
phases.text: Barrett's militia advanced on the bridge and exchanged fire with Laurie's companies, who broke and fled to the grenadiers coming from the town. This isolated the four companies at the farm.
phases.quote: the British abandoned their wounded. They fled to the safety of grenadier companies coming from the town center.

phases.title: The column leaves Concord and is hit on the road
phases.text: Parsons' companies returned to the town and the Regulars marched east. Militia converged on the road and the British charged up Brooks Hill, but the colonists held it and inflicted heavy casualties on the attackers.
phases.quote: Smith's leading forces charged up the hill to drive them off, but the colonists did not withdraw, inflicting significant casualties on the attackers.

phases.title: Percy's brigade rescues the column at Lexington
phases.text: Near the Lexington line Parker's men, some bandaged, ambushed the column from a hill, and Smith was wounded. Percy's brigade arrived with artillery and fired at extreme range, dispersing the pursuing militia.
phases.quote: Percy ordered his artillery to open fire at extreme range, dispersing the colonial militiamen.

phases.title: Percy's column fights its way to Charlestown
phases.text: The combined column set out with flankers on both sides and the rearguard rotated. Militia fought it all along the road, notably at Jason Russell's farm in Menotomy. Percy turned onto a track to Charlestown, and the circle of fire was broken.
phases.quote: Percy directed his troops down a narrow track (now Beech Street, near present-day Porter Square) and onto the road to Charlestown.
